significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: the “internal harmfulness-recognition signal” and especially its drift velocity forecast later behavioral alignment collapse with usable lead time, while conditional anchoring can preserve safety with less utility loss than continuous constraints. This establishes both a temporal phenomenon and a limited mechanism/control account—progressive representational erosion precedes unsafe behavior—but it does not fully explain why the harmfulness representation erodes; it fixes expectations about future collapse and the decision to halt or correct a run, rather than merely showing that a safety direction exists. Verified false would meaningfully rule out a small fixed canary signal as a reliable leading indicator or gate, although it would not rule out progressive erosion generally; true and false are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score because generic “mechanistic LLM safety” would not imply this specific early-warning coupling.

reach.justification: The named handles are the “held-out ‘canary’ probes,” their monitored drift velocity, and the “drift-velocity-gated activation-anchoring intervention”; these are ex ante because they let an operator “halt or correct a run before it ships an unsafe model.” The hypothesis asserts use across benign, outlier-benign, and poisoned fine-tuning and presents a fine-tuning-service operator as the downstream user; after per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction is still that canary drift precedes behavioral collapse, rather than merely supplying an uninformative search procedure. Reach stops short of the top band because coverage by a tiny fixed canary set and a single harmfulness direction may be category- and model-fragile, but the topic-substitution check confirms that the ex-ante monitor-and-gate handle—not the generic importance of LLM safety—supports the above-median score.
